title: The Bronze Age
summary: The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age and preceded the Iron Age, when weapons and tools were made of bronze, an alloy of tin and copper. It began in the Near East and southeastern Europe in the late 4th and early 3rd millennium BCE, and in the Middle East lasted until about 1200 BCE. It reached other regions at different times and did not appear in Africa or Australasia.

uncertainty.note: History.com dates the Bronze Age in the Middle East and parts of Asia from roughly 3300 to 1200 B.C., ending abruptly with systemic collapse; Oxford Dictionary of Phrase and Fable (Encyclopedia.com) notes the Bronze Age began in the Near East and SE Europe in the late 4th and early 3rd millennium BC.

where.modern_name: Near East; stand-in pin at Uruk, Iraq
where.historical_name: Unug (Sumerian) / Uruk (Akkadian), Sumer, southern Mesopotamia (Early Bronze Age; city-state period)

importance.justification: The Bronze Age established metalworking technology, the earliest urban state bureaucracies, writing, and transcontinental trade routes that structured Old World civilizations for over two millennia.

related.because: The systemic crisis, warfare, and economic disintegration around 1200 BCE brought the Bronze Age civilizations of the eastern Mediterranean to an abrupt close.
